column2: Voice assistants were supposed to run the house. Instead, simple commands lag, big jobs stall halfway, and they forget what you told them.
So I built Agora Plus. A household assistant that runs on your own server, with one calm page for the whole home.
Tell it something once. It writes the fact to your household file, reads it back, and shows you a verified receipt.
Ask later, and it answers straight from memory. Simple requests never touch a model, so they come back in milliseconds.
Lists and reminders live on the same page. Add things by voice, and tick them off by hand.
The morning briefing leads with what matters most. Allergies, medicine, and what's due today.
Bigger jobs become a plan you can read first. Nothing starts until a person says yes. The model can't approve itself.
Then a team of agents gets to work. Scout researches, Planner builds the list, and Keeper checks every step against what the family saved, like Mia's peanut allergy.
Every action is a real tool call over the Model Context Protocol. The same household works in Claude today, and it comes packaged as an Alexa Plus add-on.
Agora Plus. Your home assistant, upgraded. It remembers, it asks first, and it shows its work.
